text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P99 latency spike detected on continuous-batching path in us-west-2. alerting threshold crossed at 6141592610. Service: /v1/generate (streaming).

sam.oncall: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 3.6s. any customer pages yet?

olivia.support: No pages yet but one customer (AcmeHealth) reported degraded streaming during last 5m. Support is prepped to notify if we escalate.

mike.ops: grabbing perf dashboard. dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood/inference/cont-batch/usw2 (private)

mike.ops: metrics look like a tail event concentrated on streaming slots. throughput steady, but a subset of workers showing very high per-token latencies and long KV eviction times.

raj.ml: this smells like mixed-seqlen packing -> large sequences block batch for stream hedging. last deploy had packer change to favor max_utilization. Could cause large short+long combos to blow up tail.

sam.oncall: rolling back packer? risky mid-incident. any quick mitigations?

dana.sre: two quick mitigations we can try live: 1) reduce max_batch_size for streaming workers to 16 (from 64) 2) enable sequence-length-aware fairness (preemptive_shedding=true) to let short requests preempt long ones.

mike.ops: I can flip max_batch_size in the runtime config for the streaming pool. Patch will apply without restart. doing it now:

```
# runtime pool override
pool: streaming-usw2
max_batch_size: 16
apply_now: true
```

mike.ops: pushed. PCR id: pcr/614159. watching.

sam.oncall: enabling preemptive_shedding on one host group to test. this is lower risk than global change.

raj.ml: also lower kv_cache_max_entries temporarily to reduce eviction stalls; longer sequences hold large KV and cause swap churn. set kv_cache_max_entries: 64k -> 32k on streaming nodes.

mike.ops: kv change applied to canary host group.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: config change applied (max_batch_size=16) at 6141592702.

sam.oncall: early numbers: p95 down to ~280ms, p99 at 700ms on canary. promising.

olivia.support: AcmeHealth confirmed improvement on their session. They say streaming responsiveness returned to normal.

dana.sre: good. lets hold the smaller max_batch_size for 30m and monitor for regression. if stable, we'll roll to remaining streaming pool.

mike.ops: I'll prepare a gradual rollout: 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 10m windows, with automatic rollback if p99 > 1.5s.

raj.ml: follow-up: we should tune packer logic to prefer sequence-length buckets rather than pure utilization. long-term fix: add a soft cap to packing so long sequences don't pull short ones into large batches. filing a ticket.

sam.oncall: creating incident follow-up ticket: INC-614159 - cont-batch streaming tail due to packing heuristic + KV churn. includes actions: roll config, tune packer, add perf test with mixed-seqlen replay, update runbooks.

olivia.support: tagging affected customers: AcmeHealth (partial), NovaRetail (possible mid-latency). drafting customer-safe note in case we need to publicize.

mike.ops: full rollout started at 6141592799 (20%). monitoring automated thresholds.

incident-bot: :bar_chart: p99 time series: pre-change 3.6s -> canary 0.7s -> rollout 0.8s.

sam.oncall: all clear from oncall perspective in 10m if metrics remain. keeping page open for now.

dana.sre: postmortem checklist: root cause hypothesis, config diff, packer PR id, loadtest artifacts, customer impact list, mitigation timeline. assigning owners: dana (postmortem), raj (packer PR), mike (rollout + runbook update), olivia (customer comms).

raj.ml: quick dev note for packer change: prefer bucketization by seq_len quantiles and cap per-batch total_token_estimate to 2048. pseudocode:

```
# packer pseudocode
buckets = quantile_buckets(requests, key=lambda r: r.seq_len, k=4)
for b in buckets:
  pack(b, max_tokens=2048, max_items=8)
```

mike.ops: logged an ops-config-change with audit id audit/ops/614159.

olivia.support: I'll update customers on status at 30m if we still see improvement.

sam.oncall: if anything regress, page SRE immediately. otherwise, we'll resolve and file long-term work during next sprint. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: incident mitigated (partial) at 6141592888. leaving thread for post-incident handoff.
